No separate GlueX construction/approval dates are recorded: no fetched source gives them. The detector was installed in Hall D as part of the 12 GeV Upgrade.

The collaboration wiki (2026-07-23 agenda) lists GlueX-II running in 2026 and a tentative 2027 plan for GlueX-III; no collaboration membership count newer than a 2006 wiki snapshot (about 100 from 24 institutions) was found, so none is recorded.

physics_goals.quote: has been built to search for and map out the spectrum of exotic hybrid mesons using a 9-GeV linearly-polarized photon beam incident on a proton target
physics_goals.value: Search for and map the spectrum of exotic hybrid mesons

summary.plain: GlueX fires a beam of high-energy polarised photons at a hydrogen target in Hall D at Jefferson Lab to map out and search for exotic hybrid mesons, particles whose quarks are bound together with an excited gluon field.
summary.technical: Photoproduction experiment in CEBAF Hall D: a ~9 GeV linearly polarised, tagged photon beam (from 12 GeV electrons) on a liquid-hydrogen target, with a hermetic detector (2 T solenoid, straw-tube and planar drift chambers, barrel and forward calorimeters, time-of-flight) designed for amplitude analysis of light-meson spectra and the search for exotic hybrid mesons (J^PC exotics); data taking since spring 2016.

unique_capabilities.quote: The detector is nearly hermetic for both charged particles and photons arising from reactions in the cryogenic target at the center of the detector, allowing for reconstruction of exclusive final states.
unique_capabilities.value: Hermetic large-acceptance detector for charged particles and photons with a linearly polarised, tagged photon beam, allowing exclusive final states to be reconstructed
